data.title: Unit 3: The plant world
Seeds and germination
data.heading: Seeds
data.text: For most plants life begins with the germination of a seed.
The outer covering of a seed is called the seed coat. The seed coat protects the embryo from external damage.
The tissue that surrounds the embryo is called the endosperm. The endosperm provides the embryo with nutrition.
The embryo is where life starts within a seed.
The cotyledon is the seed leaf that develops from the seed after germination.
Flowering plants either have one cotyledon or two.
Some seeds have only one cotyledon and so are called monocots,
Some seeds have two cotyledons and so are called dicots,
